title: Traditional Examination Based on Ten Commandments
description: A thorough examination of conscience based on the Ten Commandments, suitable for adults preparing for confession.

categories.title: First Commandment: "I am the Lord your God, you shall not have strange gods before me."
categories.description: This commandment asks us to put God first in our lives and to avoid idolatry in all its forms.

items.text: Have I neglected to pray daily?
items.clarification: Prayer is our lifeline to God. Daily prayer helps us maintain our relationship with Him.

items.text: Have I denied my faith or doubted God's existence?
Have I dabbled in occult practices, horoscopes, tarot cards, or superstitions?
items.clarification: These practices attribute power to created things rather than to God, the Creator.

items.text: Have I been involved with New Age practices, witchcraft, or consulted psychics or mediums?
Have I put material possessions, career, relationships, or pleasure ahead of God in my life?
Have I been lukewarm in my faith or spiritual life?
Have I presumed on God's mercy by sinning deliberately with the intention of going to confession later?
Have I despaired of God's mercy or His willingness to forgive me?
Have I received Holy Communion in a state of mortal sin?
Have I deliberately omitted a mortal sin in a previous confession?
Have I failed to perform the penance given to me in confession?

categories.title: Second Commandment: "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain."
categories.description: This commandment requires us to show respect for God's name and avoid misusing it.

items.text: Have I used God's name carelessly or in anger?
Have I used Jesus' name as an expression of surprise or anger rather than in prayer?
Have I spoken irreverently about God, saints, or sacred things?
Have I used profane or vulgar language?
Have I made promises in God's name that I didn't keep?
Have I shown disrespect for priests, religious, or others consecrated to God?
Have I spoken disrespectfully about the Church or her teachings?

categories.title: Third Commandment: "Remember to keep holy the Sabbath day."
categories.description: This commandment calls us to worship God together as a community and to make Sunday a day of rest and renewal.

items.text: Have I deliberately missed Mass on Sundays or Holy Days of Obligation without a serious reason?
items.clarification: Missing Mass on Sundays or Holy Days of Obligation without a serious reason (such as illness or caring for the sick) is a mortal sin.

items.text: Have I arrived late to Mass or left early without serious reason?
Have I been inattentive, willfully distracted, or irreverent at Mass?
Have I done unnecessary work on Sundays?
Have I failed to make Sunday a day of rest, prayer, and family time?
Have I failed to dress appropriately and modestly for Mass?
Have I failed to contribute to the support of the Church according to my means?

categories.title: Fourth Commandment: "Honor your father and your mother."
categories.description: This commandment requires us to respect and care for our parents and all legitimate authority.

items.text: Have I disobeyed or disrespected my parents or guardians?
Have I neglected to care for elderly or ill parents?
Have I failed to help with household responsibilities when able?
Have I treated my children with disrespect, impatience, or excessive anger?
Have I neglected the religious education and formation of my children?
items.clarification: Parents are the primary educators of their children, especially in matters of faith.

items.text: Have I failed to spend quality time with my family?
Have I been disrespectful to teachers, employers, or others in legitimate authority?
Have I failed to foster vocations to priesthood or religious life in my family?

categories.title: Fifth Commandment: "You shall not kill."
categories.description: This commandment forbids unjust harm to human life and requires us to foster the physical, spiritual, and emotional well-being of ourselves and others.

items.text: Have I harbored anger, resentment, or hatred in my heart toward anyone?
Have I deliberately wished evil upon another person?
Have I physically harmed anyone or wished to do so?
Have I verbally abused others through insults, harsh words, gossip, or ridicule?
Have I encouraged or assisted in an abortion, or advised someone to have one?
Have I supported euthanasia or assisted suicide?
Have I abused alcohol or drugs?
Have I failed to take care of my physical and mental health?
Have I deliberately harmed myself or contemplated suicide?
Have I been reckless in driving or endangered lives through careless behavior?
Have I been uncharitable to the poor and needy?
Have I failed to forgive someone or refused to seek reconciliation?

categories.title: Sixth Commandment: "You shall not commit adultery."
categories.description: This commandment calls us to respect the dignity of our bodies, the sanctity of marriage, and the gift of sexuality.

items.text: Have I willfully entertained impure thoughts or desires?
items.clarification: Deliberately dwelling on impure thoughts rather than dismissing them.

items.text: Have I looked at pornographic material (magazines, videos, websites)?
Have I engaged in impure conversations or told inappropriate jokes?
Have I engaged in impure acts alone (masturbation)?
Have I engaged in impure acts with another person outside of marriage?
Have I been unfaithful to my spouse in thought or deed?
Have I used artificial contraception or been sterilized for contraceptive purposes?
items.clarification: The Church teaches that artificial contraception violates the procreative purpose of marriage.

items.text: Have I engaged in or supported in vitro fertilization or other reproductive technologies contrary to Church teaching?
Have I dressed immodestly or behaved in a way that could lead others to sin?
Have I failed to respect the dignity of marriage in my speech or attitudes?

categories.title: Seventh Commandment: "You shall not steal."
categories.description: This commandment requires respect for others' property and for economic justice.

items.text: Have I stolen anything or helped someone else to do so?
Have I damaged others' property without making reparation?
Have I cheated in business dealings or taken unfair advantage of others?
Have I failed to return borrowed items?
Have I wasted food or resources that could have helped others?
Have I failed to give to the Church and to the poor according to my means?
Have I been envious of others' possessions?
Have I paid my employees a fair wage?
Have I been lazy at work or school, or failed to fulfill my duties?
Have I cheated on my taxes or avoided legitimate fees?
Have I gambled excessively or irresponsibly?
Have I practiced good stewardship of creation and the environment?

categories.title: Eighth Commandment: "You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor."
categories.description: This commandment calls us to be truthful and to avoid damaging others' reputations.

items.text: Have I lied or exaggerated the truth?
Have I engaged in gossip or spread rumors about others?
Have I damaged someone's reputation through revealing their faults without necessity?
Have I engaged in slander (saying something false about someone) or detraction (revealing someone's true faults without necessity)?
Have I failed to defend someone's reputation when I could have?
Have I betrayed others' trust or revealed confidential information?
Have I been guilty of rash judgment (assuming the worst of others without evidence)?
Have I failed to speak up for the truth, especially in defense of the faith or moral values?

categories.title: Ninth Commandment: "You shall not covet your neighbor's wife."
categories.description: This commandment calls us to purity of heart and respect for the marriage covenant.

items.text: Have I consented to impure or lustful thoughts about someone who is not my spouse?
Have I been envious of others' marriages or relationships?
Have I read books, magazines, or watched movies that lead to impure thoughts?
Have I deliberately sought out impure content on television, the internet, or social media?
Have I failed to guard my senses and imagination from impure influences?
Have I failed to pray for the virtue of chastity and purity of heart?

categories.title: Tenth Commandment: "You shall not covet your neighbor's goods."
categories.description: This commandment calls us to detachment from material goods and freedom from envy and greed.

items.text: Have I been greedy or materialistic, desiring excessive wealth or possessions?
Have I been envious of others' success, talents, or possessions?
Have I been discontent with what God has given me?
Have I been jealous of others or resentful of their good fortune?
Have I failed to trust in God's providence and care for my needs?
Have I been overly concerned with material success at the expense of spiritual growth?
Have I failed to share my blessings with others in need?
Have I been ungrateful for what I have?

categories.title: Precepts of the Church
categories.description: Catholics are also called to follow these specific precepts established by the Church.

items.text: Have I failed to attend Mass on Sundays and Holy Days of Obligation?
Have I failed to confess my sins at least once a year?
Have I failed to receive Holy Communion at least during the Easter season?
Have I failed to observe the prescribed days of fasting and abstinence?
items.clarification: Ash Wednesday and Good Friday are days of fast and abstinence; Fridays of Lent are days of abstinence from meat.

items.text: Have I failed to contribute to the support of the Church according to my means?
Have I entered into marriage without following the laws of the Church regarding marriage?
